1.title: The Doll Shelf
1.text: Sabrina has gone quiet in the lounge, the way she does when the house is too loud in her head. Sam finds her in the back with her small collection of dolls lined up on a shelf. "You have been wondering whether to ask me something for nine days," she says, not turning. "Ask, or I will have to answer it unasked." Rain taps the window. Sabrina has not touched her tea, and the dolls watch with their glass eyes, as if they also know what is about to happen.

image.comp: turning from the doll shelf with one doll in her hands, deadpan expression softening, a faint almost-smile
image.setting: back room with a shelf of dolls, purple lamplight, drawn curtains

1.goRes: Her composure holds for a full second. Then she kisses back, and somewhere in the house a spoon bends itself quietly on a table.
1.waitRes: "Mm. I knew you would say that." A pause. "I did not know it would sting. Interesting." She sets the doll back on its shelf, very carefully.

2.title: Quiet Hands
2.text: Sabrina has been sitting up with Sam through a bad night of rumors and rowdy guests, shielding the whole hall from thoughts that are too loud. At last she sits beside him, takes his hand, and presses her cool fingers into his tense palm. "You are tired in four places. Allow me." She has not said a word about it, but the room is a little warmer than it was, and the candle flame has leaned toward the two of them all on its own.

image.comp: sitting close on a settee, holding his hand in both of hers, calm gaze, a faint flush on her cheeks
image.setting: dim upstairs sitting room, purple curtains, one candle

2.goRes: She finds the knots in his shoulders, then in his breath, then in his nerve. For once the quietest woman in the house does not stop him from hearing her sigh.
2.waitRes: "I decide when I have done enough." She relents, and lets her head rest on his shoulder instead. "...But this is acceptable."

3.title: Nothing Left to Read
3.text: "I cannot read you," Sabrina says at her door, lamp low. "Not truly. You are loud, and then you are not, and I cannot say which is the real you. I have decided that is the reason I want you here. Come in, Sam. Be unreadable. Be mine tonight." She has dimmed every lamp but one and set a pot of plum tea on the sill. Everything about the room says she has planned this carefully, and it is clear she is nervous.

image.comp: standing in her doorway in a plum silk robe, hair loose, steady dark eyes, one hand extended
image.setting: her bedroom, purple silk bedding, a row of dolls on the sill, candlelight

3.goRes: She closes the door with a flick of her mind and then, quite deliberately, with her hand. "Good," she whispers. "No thoughts. Only you."
3.waitRes: "I am never unsure. I am occasionally afraid. This is the second." She smiles thinly. "Take your time. I can wait; I have seen how it ends."

jump.title: All Thoughts at Once
jump.text: The roar in Sabrina's head finally breaks her calm in the kitchen at dusk. She grips the counter, then Sam's collar. "Everyone is thinking about you tonight. Everyone. I would like to be the loudest." She kisses him hard and does not stop at one. Plates rattle on their shelves. A ladle lifts an inch off its hook and settles back, which is as close to a blush as Sabrina's gift ever gets.

image.comp: gripping his collar, eyes closed, composure cracking, flushed, pulling him toward the door
image.setting: kitchen at dusk, copper pots, lamplight

jump.goRes: For once her thoughts and his are the same, and the entire house goes silent around them.
jump.waitRes: She goes still, then nods. "Yes. Breath. A stupid, wonderful idea." She counts four slow ones, still holding his collar.

1.title: A Fascinating Excavation
1.text: Cynthia has spent the week mapping the cellar of the house, convinced a very old wall sits behind the wine racks. Sam finds her dusty to the elbows, a brush in her hand and a smudge on her cheek. "Do you know what I found?" she asks. "Nothing. And I could not be happier. It is the company." She steps closer. A damp, earthy smell hangs in the cellar, and Cynthia's field jacket is draped over a crate. She has never looked less like a champion, or more like herself.

image.comp: kneeling then rising in the cellar with a brush in her hand, dust on her cheek, composed smile and warm eyes, close to him
image.setting: stone cellar lit by a lantern, wine racks, a half-cleared wall

1.goRes: She kisses like she does everything: with attention, patience and no hurry at all. Then, softly, "Fascinating. I'll have to study this further."
1.waitRes: She laughs, a rare real one. "Quite right. A champion with soot on her face. Ask me again at supper."

2.title: Ruins by Lamplight
2.text: Cynthia lays an old map across Sam's desk and lets her hand rest on his. "Legends say two travelers met on a night like this and neither went home." Her tone is academic. Her eyes are not. "I should like to test the hypothesis." Rain beats on the roof. She has brought tea in a travel flask, two mismatched cups, and a surprising number of excuses for staying until the lamp burns low.

image.comp: leaning over a desk with a yellowed map, her hand on his, composed smile with a hint of mischief
image.setting: study lit by a single oil lamp, maps and old books piled high

2.goRes: She is a careful scholar and a patient one. By the end of the evening, the map has gone to the floor and neither of them is reading.
2.waitRes: "Delightful. Then I shall gather more." She rolls up the map, unhurried. "I do not mind waiting. Waiting is most of archaeology."

3.title: The Champion Takes a Night Off
3.text: Cynthia has taken down her hair and put her coat over the chair. At her door she looks like someone who has finally closed a very long book. "I have won every title that I set out to win. This is the first thing I have wanted that I could not simply earn. Stay with me, Sam." For a long moment she says nothing. On the nightstand sits a fragment of old pottery she once told Sam was the most precious thing she owned. She has set it beside his side of the bed.

image.comp: sitting on the edge of her bed in a black silk robe, hair down, calm and a little vulnerable, hand held out
image.setting: elegant guest room, black coat over a chair, soft gold lamplight

3.goRes: "Thank you," she says, and means it more than she has ever meant a trophy. The coat stays on the chair all night.
3.waitRes: "I am rarely unsure. Tonight I am simply unused to asking." She smiles. "Take the time you need. I am very good at patience."

jump.title: Dust and Lamplight
jump.text: The dig has gone well, the wall is old, and Cynthia is far too pleased to remain a lady. She grabs Sam's hands in the cellar, laughs, kisses him, and then does it again. "I am sorry. I am not at all sorry. I have wanted to do that since the third week." Somewhere above them a guest laughs, and the sound of the house carries down the stairs. Dust still hangs in the lantern light like a handful of gold.

image.comp: laughing and breathless with dusty gloves on his shoulders, hair coming loose, radiant
image.setting: cellar after a successful dig, lanterns on crates

jump.goRes: Her composure, impeccable for years, simply abandons her. The brush rolls into a corner, forgotten.
jump.waitRes: "Of course." She presses a hand to her flushed cheek and tries to look dignified. "I am a champion. I can be slow. Watch me."

1.title: Sticky Notes
1.text: Juniper is forty minutes late to her own breakfast, three sticky notes stuck to her sleeve. Sam peels one off. It reads, in her loopy writing, "tell Sam. SOON." "Oh!" She snatches it back, pink to the ears. "That was the thing. The note was the thing. May I... could I show you instead?" Her braid is coming undone, her coat buttoned wrong, and cold toast sits forgotten on a plate. Sam realizes that this is how she looks when she has rehearsed something all night.

image.comp: holding a sticky note to her chest, flustered, glasses slightly crooked, hopeful smile
image.setting: sunny breakfast room, papers and notebooks scattered across the table

1.goRes: She kisses him lightly, then, being thorough, again. "Right. Hypothesis confirmed," she whispers. "Wonderful."
1.waitRes: "Eat! Yes! Of course." She blushes and sticks the note to his cuff. "So you remember I asked."

2.title: Field Notes
2.text: Juniper has been taking field notes on the house for weeks, and tonight the notebook is closed. She sits beside Sam on the roof ledge with a blanket and two cups of cocoa. "I keep writing your name in the margins. That is not scientifically sound. I would like to look into it." Below them the town hums, lanterns blinking on one after another, and she has labeled the cocoa cups with tiny sticky notes that read 'S' and 'J' in her loopy hand.

image.comp: sitting on a rooftop ledge wrapped in a blanket with him, notebook beside her, soft blush and a shy smile
image.setting: house rooftop under a starry sky, chimney smoke, blanket and cocoa

2.goRes: She is a careful, tender researcher. The notebook, left forgotten, blows shut in the night wind.
2.waitRes: "Notes first," she agrees, pulling the blanket over his knees. "I like that you wait. It makes me want to be worth the wait."

3.title: A Very Late Night
3.text: "I'm late," Juniper says at the door, hair down, lab coat gone. "I'm always late. I did not want to be late for this." Her hands are trembling just slightly around a cup of tea she has plainly forgotten to drink. "I would like you to stay, Sam. Please. All night, if you like." Her room is a tidy disaster of field journals and pressed leaves, and in the middle of it she has cleared exactly one chair, and set a second pillow on the bed.

image.comp: holding a teacup in the doorway of her room, hair down, glasses off, sincere and nervous
image.setting: her tidy room, books everywhere, a green lamp lit

3.goRes: She puts the cup down and, for once in her life, is exactly on time.
3.waitRes: "I'm sure of nearly everything about you." She smiles. "Take a week. I will make a very organized chart while I wait."

jump.title: Misplaced Inhibitions
jump.text: In the supply cupboard, Juniper's stack of folders topples as she reaches for a lamp. Sam catches her, and then she is kissing him with a heartfelt, scattered sort of energy. "Sorry! No, not sorry! This is probably a bad place. Is it a bad place?" The cupboard smells of ink and old paper. Muffled footsteps pass in the corridor, and she holds her breath, then giggles at herself, which is somehow worse.

image.comp: caught in his arms among fallen folders, flushed and laughing, hair a mess, kissing him
image.setting: narrow supply cupboard, shelves of paper, dim lamp

jump.goRes: Her laugh turns into a gasp, and the folders stay where they fell.
jump.waitRes: "Beds! Yes! Very sound." She takes his hand, adjusting her glasses. "Please lead. I'll get lost."

1.title: Sun Hat
1.text: Leaf comes in from a day of wandering the market lanes with her sun hat swinging from her fingers and a pocket full of pebbles. "I found a stone shaped like a heart," she says, and presses it into Sam's palm. "Every town has something that makes me stay a day longer. Here it is you. Can I kiss you? I'm asking nicely." Behind her the market stalls are folding up, and the smell of roasted nuts drifts across the street. She has been trying to decide how to say this all day, and has settled for honesty.

image.comp: holding out a small heart-shaped stone, sun hat in the other hand, windblown hair, bright hopeful grin
image.setting: sunny front steps of the house at golden hour, market lane behind

1.goRes: She kisses him like she's discovering a new route, curious and delighted, and laughs against his mouth.
1.waitRes: "That's okay!" She nods and tucks the hat back on. "Roads are long. I'll keep the stone for you until you're ready."

2.title: Off the Map
2.text: Leaf drags Sam up to the hill behind the house to watch the evening lights come on. She spreads her jacket on the grass and lies back. "I've been to so many places and none of them felt like this. Come here." She tugs him down beside her, laughing. Fireflies drift above the grass, and far off a tavern fiddle starts up. Leaf says she has seen the northern lights and the southern coast, but she has not seen a sky she wanted to stay under until now.

image.comp: lying on a spread jacket in the grass, tugging him down, wide-open happy grin, sun hat beside her
image.setting: grassy hillside behind the house at dusk, town lanterns below

2.goRes: Her hands are warm and curious, her laughter soft in the dusk. They go further than the road they know, slow and giggling.
2.waitRes: "Okay!" She rests her head on his shoulder, entirely content. "Best view I've ever had, honestly. We have all night."

3.title: Journey's End, Maybe
3.text: Leaf has unpacked her bag at last. Her trainer clothes hang on a hook, the hat on the bedpost. "I never unpack," she says. "Not once, in all my travels. I did tonight. Stay with me, Sam. I think that's what it means." The window is open to the night, and a crescent moon hangs over the rooftops. She has swapped her boots for bare feet and looks lighter than Sam has ever seen her.

image.comp: sitting cross-legged on a bed in an oversized shirt, empty travel pack beside her, soft smile
image.setting: cozy attic room, travel map pinned to the wall, warm lamp

3.goRes: She curls toward him like someone who has finally decided to stop walking. "Home," she whispers, which says everything.
3.waitRes: "I've never been surer of a road in my life." She grins. "But take your time. The map isn't going anywhere."

jump.title: Shortcut
jump.text: Leaf gets lost in the corridors again and ends up in Sam's room, soaked from a rain shower. She laughs, drops her hat on his chair, and kisses him before the thought is over. "Wrong turn! Best wrong turn! Is it okay if I just stay?" Thunder rolls. She has been out all afternoon on some detour or other, and the first thing she does is look at him as if he were the end of the road she meant to find.

image.comp: shaking rain from her hair, laughing, leaning in to kiss him, wet jacket half off
image.setting: his bedroom on a rainy evening, window streaked with rain

jump.goRes: The rain keeps up all evening, and she makes no attempt to find the right turn.
jump.waitRes: "Good plan." She snatches a towel and grins over it. "Don't go anywhere. I find my way back fast."

1.title: After the Water Cools
1.text: Misty is draining the bathhouse for the night when Sam brings her a bucket of towels. She leans on her mop, hair damp, shorts rolled. "You always help. Nobody helps. Do you know how much I like that? ... I'm blushing because it's steamy in here." Nobody is fooled. A single lamp swings above the steaming pool, and the tile is wet underfoot. She has been scrubbing the same patch of floor for five minutes, and has plainly run out of excuses.

image.comp: leaning on a mop, damp hair in its side tail, blushing and defiant, stepping closer
image.setting: the empty bathhouse at closing, steam and tile, wooden buckets

1.goRes: She kisses like she battles: all in, and a little too hard at first. Then she softens and laughs against him. "Okay. That's better."
1.waitRes: "Fine," she huffs, flushed. "But you're making me wait, and I hate waiting. You owe me."

2.title: Pool Rules
2.text: After hours, Misty challenges Sam to a race across the big bath. He loses badly. She is gloating at the far edge, hair sticking to her shoulders, when she realizes how close he is. "Loser's penalty," she says, quieter. "I get to pick." The big bath glows in the lantern light, and her wet hair drips on the tile. She would rather lose a battle than admit it, but she is losing the one in her chest quite happily.

image.comp: perched on the edge of the pool in a sea-blue swimsuit, smug grin turning bashful, pulling him closer
image.setting: the bathhouse pool at night, lantern reflections on water

2.goRes: Her competitive streak melts into something a good deal softer. Water laps against the tile for a long, long time.
2.waitRes: "Hah! Coward." She flicks water at him. "Tomorrow. And I'm still picking the penalty."

3.title: Calm Waters
3.text: Misty's door is open a crack. She is sitting on her bed with her gym-leader boots lined up beneath it and her arms around her knees. "I don't do this half-heartedly," she mutters. "I just thought you should know. If you stay, I'm all in. I'd like you to stay." Behind her a little fish-shaped lamp glows on the shelf, and her gym badge hangs on the wall. She has tidied the room twice, and rearranged the pillows three times.

image.comp: sitting on the bed hugging her knees, hair loose, blunt but shy eyes, a little smile
image.setting: her small tidy room, a fish-shaped lamp, sea-blue blanket

3.goRes: She unfolds from herself, laughing at her own nerves, and pulls him down. The sea-blue blanket takes them both.
3.waitRes: "Don't ask me that like I'm fragile!" Then, quieter: "...Yes. Wait if you need to. I'll be ready."

jump.title: Cannonball
jump.text: A prank in the bathhouse goes wrong and Misty, furious and laughing, shoves Sam into the water and dives in after him. They surface nose to nose, and she kisses him before either can speak. "That was not part of the plan." Steam curls around the lanterns, and the water settles into a hush around them. She still has a handful of soap suds in her hair, and does not seem to care at all.

image.comp: treading water with her arms around his neck, wet hair plastered down, wide-eyed, flushed
image.setting: the bathhouse pool with steam rising, lanterns overhead

jump.goRes: The water goes quiet. Somewhere a bucket tips over. Neither of them notices.
jump.waitRes: "Right. Towels. I'm not a fish." She climbs out, glancing back with a very pink face.

1.title: Cleared Out
1.text: Clair has just thrown out a drunk who tried to grab a waitress. Sam finds her afterward on the back step, gloves off, jaw tight. "Do not say it was impressive. I know. I am tired of being impressive." She meets his eyes. "I would like to be someone's comfort for a minute. Is that foolish?" Cold rain drips off the eaves. She has smoothed her tunic three times and straightened her cape twice, though there is no one left to impress, except one man who has no idea what he's done.

image.comp: sitting on a back step with her gloves in her lap, proud posture slipping, vulnerable eyes
image.setting: back step of the house at night, torchlight, rain-dark cobbles

1.goRes: She kisses him with the care of a woman who has never been allowed to do it badly. When she pulls back, her cheeks are the color of her cape.
1.waitRes: Her pride flares for a moment, then fades. "Perhaps you are right. Do not mistake my patience for lack of interest, Sam."

2.title: The Dragon Tamer's Hands
2.text: Clair sits Sam down in the training yard and begins unwrapping the cloth from his sore knuckles. "You hold a quill wrongly. And a sword wrongly. And me, if you do not mind my saying, rather timidly." Her touch is precise, firm, and not at all unfriendly. Torches flicker along the fence, and her breath fogs in the evening cool. She speaks like an instructor, but her fingers linger on his wrist rather longer than any lesson requires.

image.comp: kneeling in front of him, wrapping his hand in cloth, proud half-smile, eyes lifting to his
image.setting: lantern-lit training yard, wooden dummies, evening wind

2.goRes: She teaches him exactly how she would like to be held, in a very short lesson with no patience for error. He is a quick study.
2.waitRes: "I do not repeat lessons." A pause. "...Tomorrow. Just this once. Do not make me regret it."

3.title: My Own Terms
3.text: Clair stands at her door in her midnight gown, boots off for the first time anyone has seen. "I have spent my life earning every single thing. You are the first gift I will accept. Stay, Sam. On my terms. I'll be gentle about the terms." She has taken the gold clasps from her hair and laid them in a row on the dresser, as if putting down arms. Tonight, there is no tamer, no gym leader. There is only Clair.

image.comp: standing barefoot in a midnight-blue gown at her door, hair half-down, chin lifted but eyes soft
image.setting: her formal bedroom, gold-trimmed hangings, candles lit

3.goRes: She locks the door with a firm click and finally allows herself to be unguarded, which is an honor in itself.
3.waitRes: "Do not insult me." Then, softer: "I am. Ask me again in a few days, if you must. The answer will be unchanged."

jump.title: Provoked
jump.text: A guest sneers that the house is no place for a proud woman, and Clair's temper breaks. After she throws him out, she turns, finds Sam beaming, and grabs him by the lapels. "Don't smirk. I'm still furious." She kisses him furiously. The slammed door still shakes on its hinges, and a few startled guests have gone quiet. Her cape is hanging crooked and her breath is coming in short, furious gasps.

image.comp: gripping his lapels, flushed and fierce, chin up, pulling him in to kiss him
image.setting: entrance hall after a scuffle, door still swinging, lamps flickering

jump.goRes: Her fury turns into something else entirely, and she keeps hold of him like she is afraid he will leave.
jump.waitRes: "I am breathing!" She catches herself, breathes, and glares at the ceiling. "...Slowly. As you wish."

1.title: Spilled
1.text: Flannery is pouring a round of drinks when her elbow knocks the whole tray into Sam's lap. "Oh no. Oh no, oh no, I'm so sorry!" She dabs at him frantically with her apron, notices where her hands are, and goes red. Then she kisses him, mostly to end the awkwardness. The tavern is nearly empty, the lamps are low, and a string of dried peppers sways above the bar. She has been dropping things all night, which she never does when she's calm.

image.comp: dabbing at his front with an apron, mortified red cheeks, leaning in for an impulsive kiss
image.setting: lively tavern floor after closing, spilled drinks, lantern light

1.goRes: She kisses him again, properly this time, and her hands finally stop flapping. "Okay. That went better than the tray."
1.waitRes: "Right! Mop! On it!" She sprints off, and looks back twice. Still pink.

2.title: Heat of the Moment
2.text: Flannery drags Sam out to the roof after closing for a dare: whoever can watch the sunrise longest without blinking. She loses in four seconds, because she is looking at him instead. "That's cheating," she mutters. "You being cute. I want to cheat back." A blanket, a jug of warm cider, and a long cold night: she has planned this whole thing, and she will deny it with her last breath. Her ears are bright red against the dawn.

image.comp: sitting close on a rooftop with a bottle of cider, red-faced, grinning, shoulder pressed against his
image.setting: tavern rooftop at pre-dawn, faint orange on the horizon

2.goRes: She is loud everywhere, except here, where she goes shy and eager at once. The sunrise happens without them.
2.waitRes: "Fine!" She laughs, a little relieved. "But next sunrise, I'm not watching it."

3.title: Hot Enough
3.text: Flannery slams Sam's door open, then closes it very gently. "I practiced a speech. It was great. I forgot it." She takes a breath. "I like you so much it's embarrassing. I'd like you to stay over tonight. Please? That's the whole speech." She has stuffed her tavern apron under his pillow, then taken it back out, then put it in again. The candle on the sill burns steady, though her hands are anything but.

image.comp: standing in his doorway, hands behind her back, fierce blush, brave grin
image.setting: his room, window open, a candle burning, night air

3.goRes: She laughs, delighted, and drags him toward the bed by both hands. Warm, loud and wholehearted, exactly as she is.
3.waitRes: "I am, but ask me again tomorrow too." She grins. "No rush. I'm slow at some things. Mostly this."

jump.title: Last Call
jump.text: The tavern empties, the last glass is empty, and Flannery, a little drunk on the night, looks at Sam over the bar. "I'm done pretending I don't think about you." She climbs over the counter, knocks over a stool, and kisses him anyway. The fire is nearly out, but the room feels hotter than it did at noon. She is a gym leader, a grandfather's heir, and the best barmaid in town, and tonight she is just a girl who is out of patience.

image.comp: climbing over a bar counter, stool toppling, laughing, flushed, kissing him
image.setting: late-night tavern bar, last candle burning

jump.goRes: She is clumsy and honest and utterly sure, and he is more than happy to be caught.
jump.waitRes: "A little." She drops onto the stool. "Fine. Water. But I meant it, and I'll say it again tomorrow."

1.title: Ribbon
1.text: May is practicing a routine in the hall, red ribbon spinning, when she trips on a rug and lands in Sam's arms mid-pirouette. She holds the pose as if it was meant. "Ta-da?" she whispers. Her face is very close. "Nobody saw. Also: I'd like a kiss, for my trouble." Late sun slants through the hall window, and a stray petal from a vase of festival flowers has landed in her hair. She has been practicing that spin for an hour, and it did not go as planned.

image.comp: mid-pirouette caught in his arms, ribbon fluttering, laughing and blushing, close to his face
image.setting: sunlit upstairs hallway, rugs, ribbon trailing

1.goRes: She kisses him lightly and then spins away, giggling, ribbon left drifting over his shoulder.
1.waitRes: "Later!" She curtsies, unbothered. "A good performer knows to leave the audience wanting more."

2.title: After the Show
2.text: After the festival night, May collapses on the dressing-room settee, shoes kicked off, ribbons everywhere. Sam brings her water. She pats the cushion beside her. "I smile at hundreds of people. The one I wanted to see smiled at me last. Come here." Her ribbons are scattered across the cushions, her shoes are on opposite sides of the room, and the faint sound of the crowd still hums in her ears. She has never looked so happy to be tired.

image.comp: sprawled on a dressing-room settee, ribbons tangled in her hair, tired glowing smile, patting the cushion
image.setting: backstage dressing room, mirror with bulbs, costumes on hooks

2.goRes: She is bubbly and a little teasing, until she is not, and her hands turn gentle in his hair. The mirror lights hum quietly.
2.waitRes: "Okay, coach." She rests her head against him with a sleepy giggle. "Rain check? Rain checks are the best part of a contest."

3.title: Encore
3.text: May's door has a paper star on it and a note: "Come in. Please. -M." Inside she sits in a white nightgown, ribbons laid out like prizes. "I wanted the last number to be just us. Stay for the encore?" There are paper stars taped all around the window, a dozen of them, each one lopsided. She made them herself that afternoon and will absolutely not admit what they are for.

image.comp: sitting on her bed in a white nightgown with her ribbons laid out, shy and hopeful smile, hands clasped
image.setting: her cheerful room, ribbons on the wall, pink lamp

3.goRes: She takes his hand and laughs when she trips over her own slippers. He catches her. Of course he catches her.
3.waitRes: "Mhm. Totally. Slightly terrified, but totally." She smiles. "Take a day or two. Encores can wait."

jump.title: Backstage Trip
jump.text: May stumbles on a cable backstage and lands on top of Sam. She does not apologize. She kisses him, upside down, laughing, and then kisses him the right way up. "That was a recovery move. This is the finish." The stage lights flicker behind them, and the last of the crowd drifts out into the night. She is still wearing her contest gown, one ribbon loose, and her laugh is the whole room.

image.comp: sprawled on top of him laughing, hair falling over his face, leaning down for a kiss
image.setting: backstage floor, cables and props, string lights overhead

jump.goRes: The next part of the routine is not rehearsed, and she improvises beautifully.
jump.waitRes: "Mm! Good idea." She hops up and offers a hand, wobbling a little. "...Don't let me trip."

1.title: Challenger
1.text: Hilda corners Sam in the hall with a grin. "Bet you can't hold eye contact for ten seconds." He can, barely. At nine she blinks, flushes, and mutters, "Cheater." Then she kisses him to make her point, loudly, and walks off. "Best of three!" Down the hall someone is clattering dishes, and a window is open on the breeze. She has been practicing that dare for days, ever since she realized she'd lose the staring contest on purpose.

image.comp: grabbing his sleeve with a competitive grin that falters into a blush, leaning up for a quick kiss
image.setting: bright upstairs hallway, doors open, laundry basket nearby

1.goRes: She was in for one. Sam hands her another, and she yelps, "Okay! Okay, you win this round."
1.waitRes: "Ha! You're on." She points a finger at his chest, grinning. Her ears are very red.

2.title: Loud Girls Go Quiet
2.text: Hilda has been boasting about her adventures all evening. At the end of the night, on the stoop, she runs out of stories and just sits. "I talk a lot so nobody notices I'm shy about the good bits." She leans in. "The good bit is you." Crickets sing in the dark. She has already told him about three towns, two rivals, and a very embarrassing fall from a bridge, but the stories have petered out, and what is left is quiet.

image.comp: sitting on the stoop with her chin on her knees, loud grin gone soft, pink boots beside her
image.setting: front stoop of the house at midnight, street lantern, quiet town

2.goRes: She is quiet for once. It does not last, but the quiet part is lovely, and so are the whispered jokes afterwards.
2.waitRes: "Aw." She smiles, ruffled but pleased, and rests against his shoulder. "A long one, then. You asked."

3.title: Winner
3.text: "I hate losing," Hilda says, leaning on Sam's door frame, hair loose. "I also hate waiting. So I'm calling it: you and me, tonight. If you say no I'll act like I never asked." Her bravado wavers. "...Please don't say no." Her pink boots are by his door, her vest is over his chair, and a handful of snacks sit on the nightstand, a clear sign she's planned this for a while and pretended otherwise.

image.comp: leaning against a doorframe in a loose shirt, cocky smile faltering, pink boots off
image.setting: his room, one lamp, bed turned down

3.goRes: She whoops, then claps a hand over her mouth, then laughs into his shoulder. The lamp goes out a while later.
3.waitRes: "Sure. Loud-sure." She grins. "Take your time. I'll bring snacks while I wait."

jump.title: Dare Accepted
jump.text: A dare at the tavern: kiss the nearest person. Hilda looks at Sam, shrugs, and does. Then she is still looking at him, and the room is quiet. "That was supposed to be a joke," she says. "It stopped being one." The whole table has gone silent, waiting for a punchline. Sam says nothing. Neither does she. Somewhere behind them, a mug gets set down very carefully on the wood.

image.comp: mid-dare grin gone sincere, hands on his shoulders, flushed, whisper-close
image.setting: tavern corner table, half-finished drinks, laughter in the background

jump.goRes: The dare is finished. A great deal of new business begins.
jump.waitRes: She exhales a laugh. "Fair. Tell me when it counts." Her grin is brighter than before.
